verdict.rationale: Gusto ships an official CLI (gusto-cli) explicitly documented as CI/agent-ready: env-var/stdin token auth for scripted environments, a stable JSON envelope (--agent/--json) auto-enabled when stdout is piped, documented exit codes, --dry-run previews, and a --confirm gate for writes — all confirmed via the GitHub repo, live install script probe, and release history (gusto-contest-61-1..6). This is strong first-party evidence of headless/CI operation, though writes are intentionally blocked pending human --confirm and the CLI can't execute actual payroll runs, limiting full unattended automation. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on confirmation of real-world CI pipelines using the CLI beyond first-party docs, and evidence the confirmation gate doesn't materially block end-to-end automated workflows.
